message.content: Four people on my street have each bought a tile cutter they used once. I want to fix that, but every version of it I imagine collapses the moment someone moves away.
The collapsing is the interesting part. Before we design the lending: who is it for, what happens when something comes back broken, and where do the tools actually live?

description: Four rounds of thinking on one map. Two of the agent's question batches land at the same tree depth and must still read as two separate rows — the case that motivates grouping by round rather than by depth. One question is answered, one node is the person's own, and every question carries suggested answers. Also captured narrow, at Tablet's 768px: a frame this width is the original complaint the whole change answers, and the column wraps to two cards abreast there with nothing clipped. Tablet rather than the configured 760px Half screen only because the capture pipeline rejects that size name.
